own_scenes.desc: Grupos muy apreciados por la subcultura por sus letras elocuentes y cargadas de sentido, una excepción en un género que no privilegia las palabras. El trío canadiense Rush, con letras del batería Neil Peart, es el ejemplo: Weinstein pasó una noche de 1982 en el aparcamiento de un estadio explicando a sus fans la historia de 2112, una teocracia que aplasta a quien quiere hacer su propia música; muchos se sabían las letras de memoria, pero más del 70 % creía que Rush estaba del lado de los sacerdotes. Geoff Tate, de Queensrÿche, es uno de los cantantes más alabados.

notes.chapter: Cap. 8: El metal en los noventa
notes.text: En los noventa se llama progmetal a grupos como Dream Theater, que incorporan elementos del jazz y recuerdan el art rock de los setenta; algunos lo combinan con el power metal.

influences.name: La edad de oro del heavy metal

refs.q: Bands such as Iron Maiden and Rush are highly esteemed for their eloquent and meaning-charged lyrics.
refs.para: The subculture’s standards for lyrics are less precise, less articulate, and less shared. Bands such as Iron Maiden and Rush are highly esteemed for their eloquent and meaning-charged lyrics. Groups such as Judas Priest are appreciated for words that give vent to the intense feelings of their fans. Nevertheless, heavy metal is not a genre that privileges lyrics and its followers do not evaluate them as elements in a coherent, fully articulated, worldview.⁷⁷
refs.chapter: Cap. 4: Disfrutar la música: parias orgullosos

refs.q: “Which side is Rush on, the priests or the dreamer who found the instrument under the waterfall?”
refs.para: As I described and then explained the story, my efforts were greeted with much enthusiasm. One fan tried to challenge my interpretation, but I was able to show him why his was inadequate. The group dispersed, but shortly afterwards someone else came up and said, “I heard that you really know 2112.” He was the first of a long line that kept me fully involved until the sun came up. I shortened the query, merely asking each the same question: “Which side is Rush on, the priests or the dreamer who found the instrument under the waterfall?” The story is about a theocracy that crushed people trying to express themselves by making their own music. Rush, proponents of romantic individualism, were undoubtedly against the priests. Each person I asked had a 50 percent chance of being right, merely by chance. Yet over 70 percent chose the priests.⁸⁴ All claimed that they knew the lyrics and many could quote them. The evidence that older listeners understand lyrics better than younger ones was not true for this group, whose ages ranged from fourteen to twenty.⁸⁵ Other interviews and conversations with metal fans, however, suggested that the general pattern (more understanding as age increases) seemed to hold true.

refs.q: Some combine power metal with progmet-al, a term used for bands like Dream Theater
refs.para: In contrast to the aggression and heavy sound of thrash and its offshoots, power metal derives mainly from classic New Wave of British Heavy Metal bands like Iron Maiden. The subgenre, famous for epic songs with spiritual themes and strong tenor vocalists, often borrows from nineteenth-century symphonic music. Helloween, from Germany, was an early exponent. Among the better-known groups are Gamma Ray, Blind Guardian, Hammerfall, Iced Earth, Jag Panzer, Stratovarious, and Angra. Some combine power metal with progmet-al, a term used for bands like Dream Theater, whose work incorporates musical elements from jazz and echoes the art rock of the 1970s.

podcast.title: Djent as a New Style
podcast.body: Djent is highlighted as a new style that emerged within the broader Progressive Metal genre, characterized by its distinctive palm-muted guitar sound. "It emerged as a new style of progressive metal, and the name comes from how guitars mute the strings with the palm of their hand to make a specific sound, like... Digent."
